references.text: Jesus had already determined to go to Jerusalem: "When the days drew near for him to be taken up, he set his face to go to Jerusalem" ([ref:Luk 9:51|Luke 9:51]). Luke 19:28 marks the final stage of this journey.

During the journey toward Jerusalem, Jesus taught in cities and villages: "He went on through towns and villages, teaching as he made his way to Jerusalem" ([ref:Luk 13:22|Luke 13:22]). Luke 19:28 shows the completion of this long journey.

Luke earlier reminds us that Jesus was traveling toward Jerusalem through the region between Samaria and Galilee ([ref:Luk 17:11|Luke 17:11]). The journey culminating in 19:28 has been a recurring theme throughout the Gospel of Luke.

Jesus foretold his suffering and death in Jerusalem: "See, we are going up to Jerusalem, and everything that is written about the Son of Man by the prophets will be accomplished" ([ref:Luk 18:31-33|Luke 18:31-33]). In 19:28 he is now about to complete this ascent.

Mark describes the same ascent to Jerusalem: "They were on the road, going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was walking ahead of them" ([ref:Mark 10:32|Mark 10:32]). The expression ἀναβαίνων εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα in Luke 19:28 corresponds to Mark's parallel description.
Matthew also states that Jesus went up to Jerusalem and foretold what would happen there ([ref:Matt 20:17-18|Matthew 20:17-18]). The ascent to Jerusalem is a common theme in all the Synoptic Gospels.

Just before, in the parable of the ten minas, it is mentioned that Jesus was near Jerusalem ([ref:Luk 19:11|Luke 19:11]). Verse 28 marks the transition from the parable back to the travel narrative, where Jesus now concretely approaches the city.

Immediately after verse 28 follows the account of the triumphal entry into Jerusalem via Bethphage and Bethany ([ref:Luk 19:29-35|Luke 19:29-35]). Jesus walking ahead of his disciples upward toward Jerusalem leads directly into this messianic entry.

Zechariah's prophecy about the king coming to Zion: "Shout aloud, O daughter of Zion! … See, your king comes to you" ([ref:Sak 9:9|Zechariah 9:9]). Jesus' deliberate ascent to Jerusalem in Luke 19:28 initiates the fulfillment of this prophecy.

The pilgrimage psalm sings of the joy of going up to Jerusalem: "I was glad when they said to me, 'Let us go to the house of the Lord!'" ([ref:Sal 122:1-4|Psalms 122:1-4]). The expression "to go up" (ἀναβαίνω) to Jerusalem reflects the Old Testament tradition of pilgrimages up to the temple city.
